name: Bankagooma
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1 languoid page and JSON for bank1258; Wikipedia 'Banka language'; Wikidata Q3438402; Semantic Scholar and CrossRef searches for 'Bankagooma'.
sources.note: Glottolog 'meds': Idiatov 2015 (phonology or text collection), Kastenholz 2002, Hochstetler 1996 (a wordlist or less). No further descriptive works surfaced by any search

sources.citation: Kastenholz, Raimund. 2025. Lexique du parler banka. Mandenkan 72: 3-44. DOI 10.4000/13ewm.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Only first-hand description of Banka. Introduction (pp. 3-5) covers nasality types, velar allophones, /d/~[ɾ], the clitic =rāN, and tone: three lexically distinctive tone levels (L, M, H); 'le système tonal de ce parler reste à étudier'. No mention of stress, accent, or prominence anywhere in the article (a full-text search for stress/accent/prosod/proémin: 0 hits).

sources.citation: Idiatov, Dmitry. 2023. La typologie aréale comme fenêtre sur la préhistoire de l'Afrique subsaharienne. HDR mémoire de synthèse, vol. 3. HAL tel-04248647.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: a full-text search for stress/accent Banka/Bankagooma/Samogo: only the bibliographic entry for Idiatov 2015 and Solomiac 2007. No Bankagooma description; nothing on Banka stress.

sources.citation: McPherson, Laura. 2020. On latent nasals in Samogo. Mandenkan 63: 68-88. DOI 10.4000/mandenkan.2314.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Comparative Samogo phonology (Jowulu, Dzuungoo, Seenku). Mentions Bankagooma once (p. 69) as 'severely underdocumented'; no Banka data, nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Hochstetler, J. Lee. 1996. Enquête linguistique sur le duungoma : une langue samogo parlée au Burkina Faso et au Mali. Mandenkan 31: 1-57 (SIL survey report dated Nov 1994).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sociolinguistic/lexicostatistic survey of Duungoma with a Banka wordlist from Zantiguila (annexe C). p. 6: 'La langue duungoma est une langue tonale, mais je n'ai pas essayé de transcrire les tons'. Nothing on stress; glottonym and vitality notes on Banka only (pp. 10-11, 29, 32).

sources.citation: Idiatov, Dmitry. 2015. Clause-final negative markers in Bobo and Samogo: Parallel evolution and contact. Journal of Historical Linguistics 5(2): 235-266.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: online with a university library login (also a publisher record (DOI), probably paywalled)
sources.note: Only Glottolog-listed descriptive source for bank1258 and the only publication by a linguist (Idiatov) with first-hand Samogo data; may include tonally marked Bankagooma examples or a footnote on prosody, though its topic is negation, not stress.

sources.citation: Solomiac, Paul. 2014. Phonologie et morphosyntaxe du dzùùngoo de Samogohiri (Mande Languages and Linguistics 10). Köln: Rüdiger Köppe.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Fullest phonology of the closest well-described sister variety (Dzuun, same Duun cluster); would supply the cluster-level prosodic profile (tone, no stress) if a proxy is ever wanted, but is not a Banka description.

sources.citation: Kastenholz, Raimund. 2002. Samogo language islands, and Mande-Senufo (Gur) interference phenomena. In Robert Nicolaï & Petr Zima (eds.), Lexical and structural diffusion: Interplay of internal and external factors of language development in the West African Sahel, 92-93, 100. Nice: Université de Nice.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Based on Kastenholz's 1999-2000 Banka fieldwork; classification/contact paper that may carry a short structural sketch of Banka (Glottolog lists it as phonology or text collection).

sources.citation: Kastenholz, Raimund. 1996. Sprachgeschichte im West-Mande: Methoden und Rekonstruktionen (Mande Languages and Linguistics 2). Köln: Rüdiger Köppe.

sources.note: Comparative-historical work that places the Duun/Dzuun/Banka group in Western Mande (pp. 70-71 per Kastenholz 2025); unlikely to discuss Banka stress but is the only other place Banka data appear.
